name: LangGraph
summary: Low-level orchestration framework and runtime for long-running stateful agents: durable execution via checkpointers, thread-scoped and cross-thread state, interrupt-based human-in-the-loop, and streaming. Its Agent Server adds an assistants/threads/runs/cron API, self-hosted or on LangSmith Cloud.

agent-runtime.note: The graph runtime executes stateful agent loops with durable execution, resuming from checkpoints after failures.

orchestration.note: Graphs mix deterministic and model-driven steps for multi-step and multi-agent workflows; the Agent Server exposes assistants, threads, runs, and cron jobs.

knowledge-memory.note: The Store persists cross-thread key-value memory with optional semantic search, but there is no built-in document ingestion or chunking pipeline.

tools-integration.note: MCP servers are usable as tools only through the separate langchain-mcp-adapters package via MultiServerMCPClient.

identity-governance.note: interrupt()/Command(resume) give real human approval gates and the Platform supports custom auth handlers with resource filters, but there is no quota enforcement or audit log.

observability.note: Tracing comes from LangSmith, a separate commercial product enabled by an environment variable, not from the LangGraph library itself.

data-secrets.note: No managed file storage or encrypted secrets store; persistence is limited to checkpointers and the key-value Store.

evaluation.note: Datasets, evaluators, and experiment runs belong to the separate commercial LangSmith product rather than LangGraph.

channels.note: No built-in Slack, WhatsApp, Telegram, or Discord gateway and no bundled chat UI; the Agent Server exposes only an HTTP API.

code-execution.note: No sandboxed code interpreter or terminal runtime; code execution must be supplied as a user-defined tool.

human-in-loop.note: interrupt() checkpoints graph state and pauses a node indefinitely, and Command(resume=value) re-invokes the same thread with the supplied value.

multi-tenancy.note: Agent Server auth handlers can attach owner metadata to threads, runs, and assistants and filter reads, but the developer writes them; there is no built-in tenant object.

declarative-deployment.note: langgraph.json declares graphs, dependencies, and environment for a single deployed application, with no plan/apply step or dependency graph between resources.

agent-versioning.note: Each assistant update creates a new version that can be promoted to active or rolled back, but there is no canary rollout or eval-gated promotion.

skill-learning.note: The Store persists data an agent can read and write, but there is no mechanism for authoring or refining reusable skills.
